explanations.explanation: Poor is the word, and it's the first one named. Isaiah 61:1 says the LORD has anointed this speaker "to preach good news to the poor." I love hearing who the good news is for. Top of the list, no fine print.

Rich doesn't show up anywhere in this verse. Isaiah 61:1 says the LORD anointed the speaker "to preach good news to the poor." I looked for rich in there like a chocolate chip in a sugar cookie, and nope. The poor are the ones named.

Kings aren't mentioned in Isaiah 61:1. The verse says the LORD anointed the speaker "to preach good news to the poor." I checked for a king twice and found zero. That's a lot of looking for a crown that isn't in the line.

Bind them up is exactly it. Isaiah 61:1 says the speaker is sent "to bind up the brokenhearted." Binding up is what you do with a scraped knee, you wrap it and hold it together. I think that sounds gentle, friend.

No testing in this verse. Isaiah 61:1 says the speaker is sent "to bind up the brokenhearted." Poking things to see if they're done is my job with cookies, not with hurting hearts. For the brokenhearted, the verse says bind up.

Nobody gets shown the door here. Isaiah 61:1 says the speaker is sent "to bind up the brokenhearted." I think binding up is about getting close, the opposite of a "Sorry, we're closed" sign. The brokenhearted are wrapped up, not sent off.

True! Isaiah 61:1 says the speaker is sent "to proclaim liberty to the captives and freedom to the prisoners." Captives and prisoners are both in that one verse. It's tucked at the end like the last cookie in the box.

This one is actually true. Isaiah 61:1 says the speaker is sent "to proclaim liberty to the captives and freedom to the prisoners." Freedom for prisoners is right there at the end of the verse. It's hiding in plain sight, like a cookie crumb on my apron.

True. Isaiah 61:2 says the speaker is sent "to proclaim the year of the LORD’s favor and the day of our God’s vengeance." Both are in the same line. That's a heavy word, so I'll let it stand just as the verse says it.

This one is actually true. Isaiah 61:2 says "to proclaim the year of the LORD’s favor and the day of our God’s vengeance." The two sit side by side in the same line. It's a heavy word, so I won't joke about it. I'll just tell you what the verse says.
Comfort is right! Isaiah 61:2 says the speaker is sent "to comfort all who mourn." And look at that word ALL. Not some, not most, not the ones who signed up early. ALL who mourn.

Correcting isn't the assignment here. Isaiah 61:2 says the speaker is sent "to comfort all who mourn." Nobody walks up to a mourner with a clipboard, friend. The verse says comfort, and it says it for all of them.

Warning isn't what mourners get in this verse. Isaiah 61:2 says the speaker is sent "to comfort all who mourn." You don't hand a hurting person a caution sign. The verse hands them comfort, and it hands it to all of them.

A crown of beauty, yes! Isaiah 61:3 says the speaker gives the mourners in Zion "a crown of beauty for ashes." Ashes go out and a crown comes in. I've got a tall white hat and even I don't get a crown, so I'd sign up for that swap in a heartbeat.

A ring of gold has a nice sparkle, but it isn't in the verse. Isaiah 61:3 says "a crown of beauty for ashes." A crown sits on the head, not on the finger. Keep that gold in your pocket and look for the crown.

As a fellow stamper, I respect the royal seal guess. But Isaiah 61:3 says the mourners in Zion get "a crown of beauty for ashes." No seal gets pressed into wax in this verse. What comes in is the crown.
Joy is it! Isaiah 61:3 says "the oil of joy for mourning." Mourning goes out and joy comes in. Joy that arrives as oil sounds like it soaks all the way in, like a warm oven in a cold kitchen.

Healing is a lovely word, but verse 3 doesn't use it here. It says "the oil of joy for mourning." Verse 1 does say the speaker is sent "to bind up the brokenhearted," so you're in the right neighborhood. The oil in this verse is joy.
Peace is a good word and it sits close to joy in my head. But Isaiah 61:3 says "the oil of joy for mourning." Joy is the one the verse names. Close, friend, and now you've got it.

Sackcloth isn't in this verse. Isaiah 61:3 says "a garment of praise for a spirit of despair." The garment is praise, and I'd say that sounds way more comfortable than sackcloth. So despair goes out and a garment of praise comes in.
False is right. Isaiah 61:3 says "a garment of praise for a spirit of despair." The garment is praise, not sackcloth. That's one outfit change I'd pay to see.

Oaks of righteousness! Isaiah 61:3 says "So they will be called oaks of righteousness, the planting of the LORD." Mourners in Zion get called oaks. An oak is the kind of tree that makes the other trees take notes.

A lily would look lovely on my counter, but that's not the name here. Isaiah 61:3 says "So they will be called oaks of righteousness." Oaks, friend. Think big, think sturdy, think a tree that has things to say.

Reeds by the water is a nice picture, but it isn't this one. Isaiah 61:3 says "So they will be called oaks of righteousness, the planting of the LORD." The oak is the one with the muscles. And the verse says the LORD is the one who planted it.

That's the reason the verse gives. Isaiah 61:3 says they are "the planting of the LORD, that He may be glorified." The oaks get the name, and the glory goes to Him. I think that's a pretty fine deal for an oak.

explanations.answer: So they may rule the nations
explanations.explanation: Ruling the nations isn't the reason the verse gives. Isaiah 61:3 says they are "the planting of the LORD, that He may be glorified." The reason named is glory for the LORD. A throne for the oaks isn't in the line.

Resting forever sounds nice, and I wouldn't mind a nap on the cooling rack myself. But Isaiah 61:3 gives a different reason: they are "the planting of the LORD, that He may be glorified." The reason the verse names is His glory. Go with the verse, friend.

Rebuild is it. Isaiah 61:4 says "They will rebuild the ancient ruins," and then it adds restore and renew. Three verbs in one verse, friend. That's a full day of work, and they're signed up for all of it.

Mourning was the thing verse 3 sent out the door. It gave "the oil of joy for mourning." Then verse 4 gets to work: "They will rebuild the ancient ruins." Rebuilding is the answer, so the hammers come out.

Walking away from a mess is a real option. I've done it with a stack of dirty mixing bowls. But Isaiah 61:4 says "They will rebuild the ancient ruins; they will restore the places long devastated." Nobody leaves these ruins behind.

True! Isaiah 61:6 says "But you will be called the priests of the LORD; they will speak of you as ministers of our God." That "But" turns the corner from verse 5 into a brand new name. I love a verse that says "But" and then delivers.
This one is actually true. Isaiah 61:6 says "But you will be called the priests of the LORD; they will speak of you as ministers of our God." The name is right there in verse 6. No hunting required.
True. Isaiah 61:6 says "you will feed on the wealth of nations, and you will boast in their riches." And look, it says boast. Out loud. I love a verse that doesn't whisper.

This one is actually true. Isaiah 61:6 says "you will feed on the wealth of nations, and you will boast in their riches." It sits in the same sentence as the priests line. Feeding and boasting are both right there in the verse.
Portion is right. Isaiah 61:7 says "Instead of shame, My people will have a double portion." Double, friend. Not a little extra, not a fair share. DOUBLE.
I think shame can feel like a burden, but that's not the word here. Isaiah 61:7 says "Instead of shame, My people will have a double portion." The double is a portion. It's a good thing to carry.

Debt is the one that stings at the end of the month, I know. But Isaiah 61:7 says "Instead of shame, My people will have a double portion." Bills have a way of doubling on their own. This double goes in the good direction.
Justice is it. Isaiah 61:8 says "For I, the LORD, love justice; I hate robbery and iniquity." Love and hate in one line, said plainly. I think it's a comfort to hear what He loves said so clearly.

Sacrifice is a real thing in the Bible, but it's not what this verse names. Isaiah 61:8 says "For I, the LORD, love justice; I hate robbery and iniquity." What He says He loves here is justice. Robbery and iniquity are on the hate side of the line.

Wealth does show up two verses back, in "the wealth of nations" (Isaiah 61:6). But verse 8 names what He loves, and it's justice. Isaiah 61:8 says "For I, the LORD, love justice; I hate robbery and iniquity." Different verse, different word.
It's the opposite, friend. Isaiah 61:9 says "Their descendants will be known among the nations, and their offspring among the peoples." Known, not unknown. So this one is a hard no.
False is right. Isaiah 61:9 says "Their descendants will be known among the nations, and their offspring among the peoples." Nations and peoples both. Nobody stays unknown in that line.

Blessed is it! Isaiah 61:9 says "All who see them will acknowledge that they are a people the LORD has blessed." Even the folks looking on have to admit it. That's a testimony nobody has to hand out flyers for.

Scattered is what my sprinkles do when I get excited, but it isn't the word here. Isaiah 61:9 says "All who see them will acknowledge that they are a people the LORD has blessed." The word is blessed. And the whole crowd of onlookers says so.

I've been humbled by a mixing bowl more than once, but that's not the word here. Isaiah 61:9 says "All who see them will acknowledge that they are a people the LORD has blessed." And verse 7 sends humiliation out, with "instead of humiliation, they will rejoice in their share." Blessed is the word.

explanations.answer: God has clothed me with salvation
explanations.explanation: Yes, the reason is in the wardrobe. Isaiah 61:10 says "for He has clothed me with garments of salvation." That's the reason the rejoicing voice gives. Hop-around joy with a reason behind it, friend.

explanations.answer: God has given me a long life
explanations.explanation: A long life is a nice thing, but it isn't the reason named. Isaiah 61:10 says "for He has clothed me with garments of salvation." The verse points at the clothes. Garments of salvation are the reason for the joy.

explanations.answer: God has made me a great king
explanations.explanation: Nobody gets crowned king in this verse. The reason given is "for He has clothed me with garments of salvation" (Isaiah 61:10). It's all about what He put on the one rejoicing. Look for the clothes, not the crown.

explanations.answer: A bridegroom and a bride dressed up
explanations.explanation: A bridegroom and a bride, you got it. Isaiah 61:10 says "as a bridegroom wears a priestly headdress, as a bride adorns herself with her jewels." Nobody shows up to a wedding in their gardening clothes. That's the picture of being dressed up.

explanations.answer: A king dressed for his crowning
explanations.explanation: A king in a crown is a good picture, but it isn't the one the verse uses. Isaiah 61:10 says "as a bridegroom wears a priestly headdress, as a bride adorns herself with her jewels." The comparison is a bridegroom and a bride. Look for the wedding clothes.

Battle gear is a strong picture, but it isn't this one. Isaiah 61:10 says "as a bridegroom wears a priestly headdress, as a bride adorns herself with her jewels." That's more jewels than armor, friend. It's dressed up for a wedding, not a fight.

Praise is right! Isaiah 61:11 says "the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring up before all the nations." Seeds in a garden don't ask permission, they just pop up. My whole planet is cookie, so a garden there would be a very sweet problem.

Peace is a lovely word, but it isn't what verse 11 says. Isaiah 61:11 says "the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring up before all the nations." The word that springs up with righteousness is praise. And it springs up before all the nations.

Plenty sounds like something a garden would bring, I'll give you that. But Isaiah 61:11 says "the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring up before all the nations." The word is praise. The garden picture is about what springs up, and the verse names it.
